[THOUGHT] The diagnosis of drug-induced akathisia is strongly supported by: (1) temporal association with risperidone initiation (~2 months), (2) classic phenomenology (subjective restlessness + objective fidgeting/pacing, diurnal variation, movement-induced relief), (3) absence of confounding EPS or mimics (e.g., no parkinsonism, dystonia, anxiety-driven restlessness, or metabolic/endocrine abnormalities per current assessment), and (4) pharmacologic plausibility (risperidone is a high-risk D2 antagonist for akathisia). While the Barnes Akathisia Rating Scale (BARS) was recommended for confirmation, it is not *diagnostically mandatory* — clinical diagnosis remains valid and widely accepted when criteria are met. All red-flag alternative diagnoses have been explicitly ruled out or deemed unsupported. Critical labs (ferritin, iron/TIBC, prolactin, risperidone level) are prudent for risk stratification and management refinement but are *not required to establish the diagnosis*, as akathisia is a clinical diagnosis. With only 1 turn remaining (15/16), and no unresolved diagnostic uncertainty or unaddressed red flags (e.g., atypical features, treatment resistance, neurological signs suggesting alternate etiology), the evidence is sufficient for definitive diagnosis.
